issues.body:
The owner needs a reliable Windows 64-bit demonstration on Thursday, 26 November 2026. This tracks the current delivery follow-up; it is not a backdated team requirement.

Acceptance:
- Extract-and-run offline package with a pinned official runtime; no installation, pip, Node.js or network needed for the presentation.
- Separate fictional demo database, first-run seed, persistent restart, exclusive launch, occupied-port recovery and confirmed backup-before-reset.
- Clear report-copy feedback and native UTF-8 Markdown download, including clipboard rejection and no-JavaScript fallback.
- Verify the extracted runtime from a Chinese/space path, native StartDemo.cmd, minimal PATH, persisted state and readable backup.
- Preserve application regression, keyboard, responsive, reduced-motion and test-only study checks. Include true logs, version hashes and offline contingency screenshots.
- A bilingual guide with four suggested presentation segments. No fabricated member activity or human evaluation outcomes.
- Preserve existing uncommitted A1 report edits; exclude user databases, study data and credentials from the ZIP.

issues.body:
The owner requested further usability improvements and dynamic effects. The existing local, server-rendered workspace keeps its teal design system and dependency-free runtime.

Acceptance criteria:

- Brief transform/opacity entrances and hover/pressed feedback preserve layout, keyboard focus and native navigation.
- The semantic seven-field completeness score updates immediately; a visual progress fill smoothly retargets during rapid edits. Missing-field links and native progress remain usable without JavaScript.
- Native create, status and filter submissions show explicit pending text, a loading indicator and disabled submit controls. Returning through browser history restores the action and form guidance.
- Selecting a status previews the pending transition and requires explicit save; selecting the current value keeps Update disabled.
- Reduced motion disables CSS and JavaScript motion, including live preference changes; static progress and pending feedback remain clear.
- Existing app and test-only study flows pass, with responsive/keyboard/no-JavaScript checks. Record the new source for the still-empty real study; preserve the old study-ready tag. No human evaluation result is inferred.

This is a follow-up UI refinement, not a new completed student contribution or a replacement for independent review.

issues.body:
## Observed behavior

Browser Back restores text/severity but leaves completeness at 0%. A report opened from filtered page 2 returns to the unfiltered first page; status redirects also discard the list context. Null characters can trigger an unhandled SQLite title constraint or persist into optional text.

## Acceptance

- Recompute live guidance, progress and code-point counter after browser-restored form values are available.
- Carry only validated severity/status/page context through list→detail→status update/conflict→Back to reports, with native links/forms and no arbitrary return URL.
- Reject invalid/duplicate navigation parameters before status mutation.
- Reject null characters as field validation, retain other inputs and leave the server healthy with no insert.
- Preserve prior fixed tags and design system; add focused regressions and archive actual results. This is technical follow-up, not a claimed extra human team iteration.
issues.title: UI-03: Restore history guidance and preserve filtered detail navigation

issues.body:
## Observed defects

- At 901px and 1120px, the Completeness header exceeds its column's content width.
- Native maxlength counts UTF-16 units while Python validates Unicode code points: 100 emoji are silently reduced to 80 in the title field, although the service permits 160. The live counter follows the wrong unit.
- A report with all text fields at valid Unicode limits is rejected with HTTP 413 before field validation because the 64KB transport bound is smaller than valid form-urlencoded input.
- Long guidance creates a nested scroll region and clipped prompts on the desktop form.

## Acceptance

Preserve 160 supplementary Unicode characters in title with and without JS; show code-point counts; reject 161 at the server while retaining input. Allow a maximal valid Unicode form within an explicit finite transport bound. Keep meaningful table headers within columns at breakpoint widths. Make guidance reachable without nested clipping, maintain keyboard order, and polish the existing teal UI. Preserve earlier report/release evidence and provide a requirement-by-requirement audit of A1/A2 gaps without fabricating human activity.

Focused regression tests are added before fixes; their observed failures and the corrected checks will be archived.
issues.title: UI-02: Fix Unicode input limits, clipped guidance and breakpoint layout

issues.body:
Audit found 9px headers / 10px badges, horizontal mobile browsing, unbounded list rendering and Python/JS whitespace disagreement. Refine the existing teal UI and preserve the seven-field reporting scope.

Acceptance: 25 reports per browser page, accurate filtered totals, stable ordering, no omissions/duplicates, filters retained in next/previous links, filter removal returns to page one. Mobile cards expose severity/status/completeness/date without document overflow. Improve typography, grouped forms and actionable guidance; retain keyboard order and no-JavaScript workflow. Unicode-only blank fields produce consistent live/server scores and cannot create blank titles. Confirm status updates and disable unchanged-value submission progressively.

Run focused and existing Python/HTTP/browser checks, desktop/tablet/mobile screenshots, selected contrast checks and the prospective bounded workload in docs/optimization/plan.md. Preserve evidence and versions. AI-assisted technical refinement does not constitute independent team review.

issues.body:
## Problem observed in I1

The 34 Python/HTTP tests pass even when the error-summary focus statement is deliberately disabled. An actual browser exercise reveals the failed criterion. The controlled mutation was restored. Evidence: `docs/a2/evidence/i1-focus-mutant.json` and the corresponding test log.

## Proposed I2 change and acceptance

Commit executable browser regression checks for the fixed common C1/C2/C3 scenarios and enable them in CI. Repeat the identical disabled-focus mutation: the new automated C1 assertion must fail while the delivered implementation passes after restoration. Record commands, exact SHAs, conditions and raw results. Add guidance/filter checks separately; compare only the shared scenarios/mutation across increments. Do not infer productivity gains from raw durations or test counts.

## Responsibility and evidence

Proposed role D (test/CI), independent reviewer B; actual members unassigned. This is AI-assisted preparation, not evidence of completed human collaboration. The A1 four-peer product study remains pending; the process measures change is justified in `docs/a2/process-improvement-plan.md`.
